parameters.content:
## Logistics Optimization Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: The WMS or e-commerce platform (Shopify, NetSuite, ShipStation) posts when a shipment is packed. A Schedule Trigger polls tracking every 30 minutes for in-flight shipments.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Customer messages for orders above a value threshold are approved by a person before sending.
   - Carrier selection rules (customer or product overrides) always win over cost.
   - Claims are drafted, not filed, until the logistics lead confirms.
   - Every selection is logged with the alternatives and prices for later audit.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/logistics-optimization/
Want it built and run for you? $247/month · custom $4,000–7,000 one-time

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Orders and shipments (WMS / Shopify / NetSuite / ShipStation)
- Carrier rate APIs and contract discounts
- Tracking events per carrier
- Measured on-time performance by carrier, service and lane
- Carrier invoices (EDI, CSV or portal export)

Select the service

Filters to services meeting the promise date with a buffer from measured on-time performance per lane, then picks the cheapest. Rules can force a carrier for certain customers or products.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Detect and explain delays" step of the Logistics Optimization Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: When a milestone is late or an exception code appears, the agent reads the tracking history and drafts a plain-language customer update and, if the carrier's SLA was missed, a claim request with the evidence.

Rules:
- Customer messages for orders above a value threshold are approved by a person before sending.
- Carrier selection rules (customer or product overrides) always win over cost.
- Claims are drafted, not filed, until the logistics lead confirms.
- Every selection is logged with the alternatives and prices for later audit.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Detect and explain delays
nodes.notes:
Detect and explain delays

When a milestone is late or an exception code appears, the agent reads the tracking history and drafts a plain-language customer update and, if the carrier's SLA was missed, a claim request with the evidence.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Detect and explain delays
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Gmail: Notify and escalate
nodes.notes:
Notify and escalate

Customer update sent from the support inbox (after a human click for high-value orders); internal alert to the logistics lead for exceptions.

nodes.name: Compare Datasets: Audit carrier invoices
nodes.notes:
Audit carrier invoices

Weekly: carrier invoice lines matched to booked shipments; differences above tolerance become dispute items with the quote attached.
